name: Smile maxxing
lead: Smile maxxing is a looksmaxxing-community term for optimising how one's smile looks, whether through teeth (whitening, alignment, cosmetic dentistry), the gums and lips, or the way the smile is expressed. Sources reviewed for this article contain no formal definition of the term, and no published research uses it.
Related topics have encyclopedic coverage: the muscles and types of smile, the perception of smiling people, and cosmetic dental procedures [1][2][3].
infobox: Cosmetic dentistry, smile training, Duchenne smile

paras: A smile is produced mainly by muscles at the corners of the mouth. A Duchenne smile also engages the muscle around the eye (orbicularis oculi), and research summarised in encyclopedias associates it with positive emotion and with being judged as more sincere [1][4]. A voluntary smile that uses only the zygomaticus major is sometimes called a Pan Am smile [1].

Smiling is reported to make a person seem more likable, approachable and, in some summaries, more trustworthy, although perception varies by culture [1][4]. Smiles were rare in Western portraiture before the nineteenth century [4].

Dental work often associated with smile optimisation includes whitening, bonding, veneers, enamel contouring, orthodontics and gum contouring [2][3]. Cosmetic dentistry is not recognised as a specialty by the American Dental Association [2].

card.summary: Forum shorthand for optimising your smile, from teeth to expression; a loose umbrella with no formal protocol.
card.note: An umbrella term; risks depend on whether it means dental procedures or expression practice.

quick.overview:
Smile maxxing is a looksmaxxing term for improving how your smile looks. It can mean dental changes such as whitening or alignment, or practising how the smile is expressed.

There is no formal definition or research using the term; it overlaps with cosmetic dentistry and smile training.
quick.mechanism: Dentally, it involves procedures that change tooth colour, shape and position. Expressively, it concerns which facial muscles are used, for example whether a smile engages the eyes (Duchenne smile).
quick.risks: Risks depend on the method. Dental procedures such as veneers can involve irreversible tooth reduction, while expression practice carries little reported risk. No studies of the term itself were found.
